papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Self-directed lifestyle interventions may improve access to weight loss care in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), but effectiveness in routine practice is unknown. OBJECTIVE: Test whether a proactively delivered self-directed lifestyle intervention improves weight and sleep-related quality of life versus usual care. METHODS: POWER enrolled patients with OSA and body mass index of 30-45 kg/m2, recruited from Veteran Affairs (VA) sites nationwide, and randomized participants to a self-directed intervention based on the Diabetes Prevention Program with video-based sessions, readings, and regular coaching reminders or usual care. Co-primary outcomes were change in Functional Outcomes of Sleep Questionnaire (FOSQ) and clinical weight in kilograms (kg) from baseline to 12 months post-randomization. Given two primary outcomes, we defined significance at p = 0.025. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: This trial randomized 696 participants. Mean age was 56.2 years (SD 12.2), with 19.7% identifying as female. Clinical weights at 12 months were available for 81.9% of intervention and 83.6% of control participants. Unadjusted weight declined 2.1 kg (SD 6.8) in intervention and 0.9 kg (SD 5.9) in control (adjusted between-group difference: -1.1 kg, 95%CI -2.0, -0.1; p = 0.037). FOSQ measures were available at 12 months for 78.2% of intervention and 90.5% of control participants. From baseline to 12 months, unadjusted FOSQ improved 1.4 (SD 2.7) points in intervention and 0.9 (SD 2.9) points in control (adjusted between-group difference: 0.6 points, 95%CI 0.2, 1.0; p = 0.001). CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: Among participants with OSA and obesity, a self-directed lifestyle intervention did not improve weight loss and led to improvements in sleep-related quality of life that are of limited clinical importance. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov NCT05104450, registered 10/19/2021.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) is the accepted first-line treatment for insomnia, but its scalability and safety in patients with co-morbid insomnia and obstructive sleep apnea (COMISA) remain unclear. Clinician-guided digital CBT-I (D-CBT-I) is a potential treatment option that may address these limitations in COMISA. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effectiveness of clinician-guided D-CBT-I versus sleep hygiene education (SHE) in patients with COMISA. METHODS: This randomized trial (n = 88) compared clinician-guided D-CBT-I (6 weekly online sessions: sleep restriction, sleep hygiene, stimulus control, cognitive restructuring, relapse prevention) with SHE alone. Blinded outcome assessments were conducted at baseline, posttreatment (6 weeks), and 3-month follow-up. Primary outcomes were Insomnia Severity Index (ISI) and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) scores at posttreatment and 3-month follow-up. Secondary outcomes included daytime sleepiness, sleep parameters, OSA severity, neurocognitive function, and adverse events. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: At 3-month follow-up, intention-to-treat analysis showed significantly greater improvements with D-CBT-I versus SHE on ISI (-9.5 vs. -4.0 points; d = -1.18, P = 0.001) and PSQI (-4.9 vs. -1.8 points; d = -0.87, P = 0.001); D-CBT-I also reduced subjective sleepiness (Epworth Sleepiness Scale; -3.4 vs. -1.0 points; d = -0.68, P < 0.001). At posttreatment, D-CBT-I reduced the apnea-hypopnea index (attended in-laboratory polysomnography; -6.0 vs. +2.0 events/h; d = -0.64, P = 0.019). Although transient increases in ESS occurred at weeks 2-4, no functional impairment or sleepiness-related adverse events were reported. Additional benefits were observed in metacognition and executive function. CONCLUSION: Clinician-guided D-CBT-I improved insomnia and OSA severity, and enhanced cognitive function in COMISA patients. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry; NO.: ChiCTR2500099854; URL: https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=267457.

papers.abstract_en: The clinical adoption of deep learning in pathology is largely hindered by the "black box" nature of current models, which often obscure the biological basis of prognosis. Here, we introduce MorphX, an interpretable framework that predicts patient survival by explicitly decoding multi-scale morphological patterns from whole-slide images. Unlike conventional methods relying on latent features, MorphX fuses macro-scale tissue texture with micro-scale nuclear metrics to attribute risk to interpretable biological phenotypes. In a multi-center study spanning 1,067 patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), MorphX achieves concordance indices of 0.775-0.799 in discovery cohorts. Crucially, we derive eight distinct morphology-based biomarkers-driven by texture heterogeneity in necrotic regions, lymphocyte density, and nuclear shape-that demonstrate reproducible survival associations across independent cohorts, offering a granular resolution of tumor aggressiveness that transcends traditional histological grading. By translating opaque computational predictions into validated biological insights, MorphX supports trustworthy, transparent, artificial intelligence (AI)-driven precision oncology.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Chlorhexidine (CHX) has been a long-standing component of oral-care bundles for preventing ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP), but recent evidence has questioned its benefit in non-cardiac-surgery ICU. We evaluated whether adding 0.12% CHX to standardized oral-care bundle provides incremental benefit in a mixed medical ICU. METHODS: We conducted a prospective, pragmatic cluster-randomized crossover (AB/BA) trial in six adult medical ICUs of a single tertiary-care academic hospital in Bhubaneswar, India. ICUs were randomized as three ICUs of two Period of 9 months with the multicomponent oral-care bundle without chlorhexidine and three with the same bundle plus 0.12% chlorhexidine with a 1-month wash-in and re-training interval. Consecutive adults ventilated for ≥ 48 h were included. The primary outcome was VAP incidence density (Clinical Pulmonary Infection Score (CPIS) > 6) as per 1,000 ventilator-days. Secondary outcomes were 28-day all-cause mortality, duration of mechanical ventilation, ICU length of stay, 28- day ventilator-free days, Beck Oral Assessment Scale (BOAS) and Critical-Care Pain Observation Tool (CPOT) scores. The primary model was a population-averaged Poisson generalized estimating equation (GEE) and adjustment for treatment, period, sequence, age, sex, APACHE II, and SOFA. RESULTS: A total of 1,035 patients (637 No CHX, 398 CHX) accrued 10,024 ventilator-days (5,918 vs. 4,106). Groups were well balanced at baseline (mean age ≈ 55 years; APACHE II ≈ 19.6; SOFA ≈ 13.4). VAP occurred in 100/5,918 ventilator-days (16.9 per 1,000) vs. 77/4,106 (18.8 per 1,000) (No CHX vs. CHX). The adjusted Poisson incidence rate ratio was 1.08 (95% CI 0.84-1.38; p = 0.56). 28-day mortality was 28.7% vs. 26.4% (no CHX vs. CHX) (adjusted OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.65-1.15; p = 0.33). ICU length of stay was longer in the CHX arm (adjusted mean difference + 0.89 days, 95% CI + 0.19 to + 1.58; p = 0.013). BOAS and CPOT scores did not differ. CONCLUSIONS: In this trial, adding 0.12% chlorhexidine to a standardized oral-care bundle did not reduce VAP incidence density or 28-day mortality and was associated with a modest increase in ICU length of stay. Routine CHX use provided no clear incremental benefit in a mixed medical ICU population. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Trials Regisrty- India (CTRI) identifier [CTRI/2024/02/062201], registered [01 February 2024].

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Depemokimab is the first ultra-long-acting biologic, with enhanced interleukin-5 binding affinity, high potency, and extended half-life, enabling twice-yearly dosing. The double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3a SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 studies demonstrated depemokimab efficacy and safety over 52 weeks in patients with asthma with type 2 inflammation and an eosinophilic phenotype. Here, we present long-term safety and efficacy outcomes over the 52-week, phase 3a open-label extension (OLE) of SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 (AGILE) alongside an integrated post-hoc analysis of the 104-week SWIFT and AGILE period. METHODS: In SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2, patients (aged ≥12 years) with asthma with type 2 inflammation, an eosinophilic phenotype (≥150 cells/μL at screening or ≥300 cells/μL during the previous 12 months), and a history of at least two exacerbations in the previous 12 months despite receiving medium-dose or high-dose inhaled corticosteroids were randomly assigned (2:1) to subcutaneous depemokimab 100 mg or placebo every 26 weeks in addition to standard of care for 52 weeks. Patients who completed SWIFT-1 or SWIFT-2 could join the single-arm, 52-week AGILE OLE study, conducted at 156 centres across 14 countries. Patients continued depemokimab (depemokimab-depemokimab group) or switched to depemokimab from placebo (placebo-depemokimab group). The primary endpoints for the 52-week AGILE OLE period were the incidence of adverse events and serious adverse events, and immunogenicity as measured by the presence of anti-drug antibodies and neutralising antibodies. Secondary efficacy outcomes, including exacerbation rate, St George's Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ) total score, Asthma Control Questionnaire-5 (ACQ-5) score, and pre-bronchodilator forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1), were also assessed. Additional post-hoc analyses were carried out to assess safety and efficacy over the 104-week integrated SWIFT and AGILE analysis period. AGILE OLE is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05243680. The SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 trials are registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04719832 and NCT04718103. FINDINGS: Between March 1, 2022, and May 19, 2025, 629 patients were included in the AGILE OLE study (419 patients in the depemokimab-depemokimab group and 210 patients in the placebo-depemokimab group). During the 52-week AGILE OLE period, adverse events occurred in 297 (71%) of 419 patients in the depemokimab-depemokimab group and 146 (70%) of 210 patients in the placebo-depemokimab group; serious adverse events were infrequent (37 [9%] of 419 in the depemokimab-depemokimab group and 19 [9%] of 210 in the placebo-depemokimab group), with no treatment-related or fatal serious adverse events reported. In the depemokimab-depemokimab group, the reduced annualised exacerbation rate was sustained over 2 years (0·51 [95% CI 0·43-0·61] in the 52-week SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 period and 0·56 [0·47-0·66] in the AGILE OLE). Improvements in SGRQ total score, ACQ-5 score, and FEV1 were maintained over 2 years. In the placebo-depemokimab group, improvements in clinical outcomes were observed after the switch to depemokimab during the AGILE OLE. INTERPRETATION: Twice-yearly depemokimab was well tolerated and demonstrated sustained efficacy over the 2-year SWIFT and AGILE period, supporting its long-term therapeutic benefit and safety profile. papers.abstract_en: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) improve outcomes across several cardiometabolic conditions, but their role in World Health Organization group 1 pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) remains uncertain. We conducted a retrospective, single-center cohort study of adults with group 1 PAH. Patients prescribed SGLT2i were compared with patients without exposure. Propensity-score matching was performed 1:2 using age, sex, baseline REVEAL Lite 2 risk category, diabetes mellitus, and statin use. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality, and the secondary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events. Associations were evaluated using fixed-exposure and start-stop time-varying Cox models. The matched cohort included 366 patients: 122 (33%) receiving SGLT2i and 244 (67%) controls. Most patients were classified as high risk by REVEAL Lite 2 (106 SGLT2i recipients (87%) and 215 controls (88%), respectively). In the fixed-exposure analysis, SGLT2i use was associated with lower mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 0.53; 95% CI, 0.31-0.91; P=.018), without a significant difference in major adverse cardiovascular events (HR, 1.23; 95% CI, 0.93-1.63; P=.14). In the time-varying analysis, SGLT2i exposure was not significantly associated with mortality (HR, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.26-2.11; P=.57). The apparent survival association was attenuated after accounting for treatment timing, demonstrating the sensitivity of observational PAH estimates to exposure classification and supporting prospective randomized trials.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer associated with cystic airspaces (LCCA) is an increasingly recognised yet under-characterised presentation of non-small cell lung cancer, accounting for approximately 1-4% of cases. Despite growing awareness driven by thin-section computed tomography and lung cancer screening, LCCA remains absent from major international guidelines and classifications, including those of the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence, the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer, and the World Health Organization. This narrative review synthesises the available evidence to define LCCA as a distinct clinico-radiological entity and to inform future guideline development. LCCA presents heterogeneously, with thin- or thick walled cysts, unilocular or multiloculated morphology, and variable solid components, frequently mimicking benign cysts, bullae, or emphysema. Such ambiguity contributes to diagnostic delay; in the NELSON screening trial, LCCA accounted for 22.7% of missed or delayed diagnoses. Several radiological classifications, notably that of Mascalchi, aid description and risk stratification. Conventional staging is problematic, as measurement of the solid component alone may underestimate true tumour extent, while fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography carries a high false-negative rate. Tissue sampling is similarly complicated by low diagnostic yield and false negative results, underscoring the importance of multidisciplinary team discussion. The natural history follows a stepwise progression from thin-walled cyst to wall thickening, mural nodularity, and invasive disease, with prognosis determined principally by stage, although mural nodularity and increasing solid components confer higher recurrence risk. Treatment broadly mirrors that of solid lung tumours; current guidance advocates targeting the whole cystic lesion for radical therapy rather than the solid component alone, with systemic anticancer therapy appropriate in advanced or multifocal disease. papers.abstract_en: Rapid pathogen identification is critical for timely antibiotic therapy in patients with pneumonia, yet current methods remain too slow or complex for routine clinical use. Here, we describe a localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR)-based biosensor platform that detects Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria directly in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) without nucleic acid extraction or amplification. Gold nano-islands (AuNIs) functionalized with antibodies against lipoteichoic acid (LTA) or lipopolysaccharide (LPS) enabled selective bacterial capture. The sensor achieved a refractive index resolution of 8.52 × 10-8 RIU with good reusability and dynamic range. Detection limits reached the concentration of 0.027 μM for purified LTA and 0.208 endotoxin units (EU) for LPS. When tested with Escherichia coli in artificial samples, the LPS sensor showed a reproducibility standard deviation (RSD) of 3.14%, detecting bacterial growth significantly earlier than conventional OD600 measurement. In 33 clinical BALF samples, sensor results correlated strongly with standard diagnostics (Pearson r = 0.963) and distinguished infected from noninfected cases using cutoff values of 0.060 rad (Gram-positive) and 0.083 rad (Gram-negative). The platform detects polymyxin B susceptibility 8 h earlier than conventional OD600 measurements, and a proof-of-concept sandwich immunoassay enables species-level discrimination between E. coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae. With excellent reproducibility (RSD = 3.14%), reusability over six cycles (84.21% ± 2.03% signal retention), and four-week storage stability (98.63% ± 5.42%), this LSPR platform offers a practical, rapid approach for frontline bacterial screening and accelerated antibiotic stewardship in pneumonia.

papers.abstract_en: Programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1) immunohistochemistry, the current standard biomarker for predicting response to programmed death protein 1/PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitors in non-small cell lung cancer, has moderate predictive value among others because of tumor heterogeneity and limited biopsy representation, whereas PD-L1 PET/CT using 18F-BMS-986192 enables noninvasive, whole-tumor assessment of PD-L1 expression and heterogeneity, potentially improving prediction of response to immunotherapy. Methods: In this prospective multicenter biomarker exploration study, patients with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer eligible for nivolumab-based therapies underwent baseline 18F-BMS-986192 PET/CT, 18F-FDG PET/CT, and tumor biopsy for PD-L1 immunohistochemistry before treatment initiation. The primary endpoint was durable clinical benefit, defined as progression-free survival (PFS) of 9 mo or greater, with secondary analyses assessing associations among tracer uptake, PD-L1 expression, survival outcomes, and PET-based radiomic features. Results: Of 91 enrolled patients, 77 were included in the final analysis of 18F-BMS-986192 PET/CT. Although PD-L1 immunohistochemistry did not differ between patients with PFS of less than 9 mo versus 9 mo or greater, PD-L1 PET uptake in lung lesions was significantly higher in patients with PFS of at least 9 mo (P = 0.01). Using an optimal mean SUVpeak cutoff of 2.4, PD-L1 PET demonstrated a high negative predictive value (94%) for durable clinical benefit, with significant associations for both PFS and overall survival, particularly in patients receiving first-line treatment. Tracer uptake showed no correlation with 18F-FDG uptake. Conclusion: 18F-BMS-986192 PET/CT revealed interpatient PD-L1 variability. Low uptake in lung lesions predicted poor outcomes with high negative predictive value. 18F-BMS-986192 PET/CT demonstrated stronger negative predictive value than did baseline PD-L1 immunohistochemistry in this cohort. These findings require prospective validation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Relapsed/refractory (R/R) lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains a clinical challenge with limited therapies and poor prognosis. CAR‑NK cell therapy has shown promise in solid tumors, but its efficacy is limited by both the availability of effective targets and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. CD73 (NT5E), highly expressed across solid tumors, catalyzes adenosine production to drive immunosuppression, representing both a specific CAR‑NK target and a key leverage point to overcome tumor immune evasion. However, its systematic evaluation as a therapeutically actionable target for CAR‑NK cell therapy in R/R LUAD remains unexplored. METHODS: We first characterized CD73 expression through integrative analysis of public datasets, primary and relapsed clinical LUAD specimens, and LUAD cell lines derived from primary and metastatic tumors. We then constructed CD73‑CAR‑NK cells and assessed their in vitro cytotoxicity across LUAD cell lines of varying malignancy, as well as their effects on extracellular adenosine and resistance to adenosine‑mediated immunosuppression. Finally, we assessed their antitumor efficacy in a stepwise manner across a tiered panel of in vivo models, including cell line‑derived xenograft (CDX), metastasis, patient‑derived xenograft (PDX), and clinically relevant immune‑humanized PDX models. RESULTS: CD73 expression was elevated in metastasis-derived LUAD cell lines and R/R LUAD specimens. Accordingly, CD73-CAR-NK92 cells exhibited potent cytotoxicity against CD73-high LUAD cells, accompanied by an activated effector phenotype, reduced extracellular adenosine, partial resistance to adenosine-mediated suppression, and limited activity toward normal bronchial epithelial cells. Notably, this enhanced function was consistently observed across multiple NK cell sources including peripheral blood-derived NK (PBNK), umbilical cord blood‑derived NK (UBNK), and iPSC-derived NK (iNK). In vivo, CD73‑CAR‑NK92 cells significantly suppressed tumor growth and metastasis, with enhanced tumor‑site enrichment, prolonged retention, and elevated intratumoral levels of TNF‑α and IFN‑γ. Importantly, in an immune‑humanized PDX mouse model, CD73‑CAR‑NK92 cells significantly reduced the growth of R/R patient‑derived xenografts, accompanied by immune remodeling, without marked systemic inflammation during the observation period. CONCLUSIONS: These findings provide preclinical evidence that CD73-CAR-NK cells exhibit potent antitumor efficacy for R/R LUAD through their dual functions of eliminating CD73-high tumor cells and resisting adenosine-mediated immunosuppressive signaling, supporting their therapeutic potential.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Intraluminal obstruction produces chronic airway epithelial hypoxia. We investigated how chronic airway epithelial hypoxia and inflammatory stimuli interact in human bronchial epithelial (HBE) cultures and resected human bronchiectatic lungs to produce an airway epithelial environment characteristic of muco-obstructive disease. MATERIALS AND METHODS: HBE cultures were exposed to normoxia or hypoxia (1% O2) for 5 days, followed by administration of supernatants from cystic fibrosis (CF) lung-derived mucopurulent material (SMM) or PBS for 24 h. A reverse order protocol with SMM followed by hypoxia was also performed. Bulk RNA-sequencing and functional (Na+ transport) studies were performed. HIF1A and EPAS1-mediated transcriptional responses were characterised in CRISPR knockdown HBE cells. RNA in situ hybridisation studies of excised bronchiectatic lungs and bioinformatic analyses of published datasets tested for relevance of in vitro findings to in vivo conditions. RESULTS: Hypoxia and SMM regulated largely separate airway epithelial transcriptional programmes regardless of treatment order. PTGS2 (COX-2), CCL20, MUC5B, and CXCL8 (IL-8) represented a small number of genes upregulated by both hypoxia and SMM. HIF1A knockdown and EPAS1 knockdown produced distinct, often opposing, effects on hypoxia-responsive pathways. HIF1A dominated upregulation of glycolytic pathway signalling. EPAS1 regulated genes that increase mucus concentration under hypoxia (e.g., SCNN1G). An EPAS1 inhibitor blocked hypoxia-induced upregulation of Na+ transport. CONCLUSION: Chronic hypoxia and inflammation regulated distinct genes/pathways that combine to produce a complex diseased environment in muco-obstructed airway epithelia. HIF1A and EPAS1 regulated distinct hypoxia-induced transcriptional responses. EPAS1 inhibition may exhibit a favourable therapeutic ratio for treatment of muco-obstructive lung diseases.

papers.abstract_en: Cisplatin resistance is a major obstacle in the treatment of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). To address this challenge, we screened a U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved drug library and identified fingolimod, an immunomodulatory agent, as a potent inhibitor of cisplatin-resistant ESCC cells. Fingolimod is likely to directly binds to Glu266 of the nuclear pore complex protein NUP54, promoting its proteasomal degradation. This disrupts the NUP54-NUP58-NUP62 central channel, impairing the nuclear import of the key DNA repair protein SPIDR. Consequently, fingolimod treatment inhibits the recruitment of the SPIDR-RAD51-DMC1 complex by chromatin, causing defective homologous recombination repair, accumulation of DNA damage, and ultimately, the reversal of cisplatin resistance. In addition, fingolimod restored the sensitivity of cisplatin to ESCC treatment in both patient-derived xenograft and organoid models. Our study unveils a novel mechanism by which fingolimod targets the nuclear pore complex to suppress DNA repair, providing a compelling rationale for repurposing fingolimod as a combination therapy to overcome cisplatin resistance in ESCC.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Rapid and comprehensive detection of respiratory pathogens is essential for immunocompromised patients with suspected pneumonia. Conventional diagnostic methods are limited in scope, often slow, and lack sensitivity, leading to reduced diagnostic yield. OBJECTIVES: To analytically and clinically validate a microbial cell-free DNA (mcfDNA) sequencing assay for bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) that enables broad and sensitive detection of pathogens causing pneumonia in immunocompromised patients. METHODS: The BALF-mcfDNA assay detects more than 500 bacteria, DNA viruses, fungi, and parasites. Analytical validation used 324 contrived samples containing DNA from 11 representative organisms and 1,294 in-silico samples. Clinical validation compared BALF-mcfDNA sequencing with usual care (UC) testing in 118 immunocompromised adults with suspected pneumonia. An independent expert panel adjudicated the etiologic diagnoses. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: BALF-mcfDNA testing demonstrated high inclusivity (97%), exclusivity (96%), and precision (coefficient of variation < 15%), with linear quantification across four orders of magnitude. Limits of detection were consistent across taxa, GC content, and genome size. In clinical evaluation, BALF-mcfDNA sequencing identified probable pneumonia pathogens in 34% of participants versus 24% for UC testing, increasing diagnostic yield by 43% (57% when combined with UC). In 24% of concordant cases, mcfDNA sequencing provided additional clinically relevant information by identifying new or species-level pathogens. CONCLUSIONS: BALF-mcfDNA sequencing enables sensitive, comprehensive, and rapid pathogen detection from BALF specimens, outperforming conventional methods and improving etiologic diagnosis of pneumonia in immunocompromised hosts.

papers.abstract_en: Capillary leak syndrome (CLS) is a rare but potentially life-threatening condition characterized by generalized edema, hypotension, and hypoalbuminemia. Amivantamab has recently been approved for the management of metastatic NSCLC. Although peripheral edema has been reported with amivantamab, CLS has not previously been described in association with this treatment. Herein, we report a case of CLS attributed to amivantamab that resolved after drug discontinuation and a short course of high-dose intravenous immunoglobulin administration. The anti-inflammatory, neutralizing, and antibody clearance-accelerating effects of intravenous immunoglobulin may explain their potential efficacy in treating amivantamab-induced CLS. As therapeutic antibodies become increasingly used, CLS may be encountered more frequently. A better understanding of its pathophysiologic characteristics is therefore essential to develop effective treatments and preventive strategies, ultimately minimizing its consequences on patient outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), the predominant subtype of non-small cell lung cancer, is characterized by high incidence, poor prognosis, limited therapeutic efficacy. Glycolysis-high LUAD is associated with aggressive tumor behavior and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) that broadly impairs anti-tumor immunity and therapeutic efficacy. Effective strategies targeting this metabolically aggressive phenotype are urgently needed. In this study, we developed a combination strategy that modulates DEPDC1-associated glycolysis by integrating fluvastatin (Fluv) with an integrin αVβ3-targeted photodynamic nanoplatform (cRGD-TPA-DCR-NP, with light irradiation; NPL), termed Fluv + NPL. Integrated multi-omics analyses, together with Western blotting and glycolytic rate (GlycoPER) measurements, demonstrated that Fluv + NPL suppressed DEPDC1-mediated NF-κB signaling, thereby inhibiting PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway activity and reducing glycolytic metabolism in LUAD cells. Simultaneously, Fluv + NPL downregulated exosomal CCL2 levels and inhibited M2 macrophage polarization. In vivo studies further showed that Fluv + NPL effectively modulated the immune microenvironment of LUAD, as evidenced by enhanced M1 macrophage polarization, increased infiltration of effector T cells, and reduced M2 macrophage abundance, ultimately resulting in significant inhibition of LUAD growth. Collectively, our findings reveal an important role of DEPDC1 in linking glycolytic metabolism to immune regulation and establish Fluv + NPL as a promising therapeutic strategy that simultaneously suppresses glycolysis and enhances antitumor immunity through modulation of DEPDC1. These results provide new insights into glycolytic metabolism-immunity-based combination therapies for LUAD.

papers.abstract_en: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) promotes tuberculosis pathogenesis in part by exploiting host pyroptosis, yet bacterial factors that directly engage the pyroptotic executioner machinery remain poorly defined. Here we identify the ESX-5 component EccB5 as a mycobacterial virulence factor that binds gasdermin D (GSDMD) and potentiates pathogenic pyroptosis. In vivo, conditional ATc-inducible knockdown of eccB5 in the Mtb H37Rv strain markedly reduces lung pathology, bacterial burden, and host cell death in mice. Conversely, ectopic expression of EccB5 in nonpathogenic Mycobacterium smegmatis is sufficient to trigger robust macrophage pyroptosis and amplify inflammatory responses in mice. Mechanistically, EccB5 enhances canonical inflammasome-associated GSDMD processing and promotes NLRP3-dependent GSDMD-N membrane association and oligomerization, without evidence of caspase-3/GSDME activation or noncanonical inflammasome engagement. Genetic ablation of host GSDMD abolishes EccB5-driven pyroptotic responses, establishing GSDMD as an essential host target. Together, these findings define an ESX5-linked virulence axis that directly couples mycobacterial infection to the execution phase of pyroptosis, thereby facilitating Mtb dissemination and disease progression. Targeting the EccB5-GSDMD interface provides a mechanistically grounded strategy for host-directed therapy in tuberculosis.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The updated New Zealand asthma guidelines in 2020, aligning with global asthma guideline recommendations, advocated for a fundamental shift from short-acting β2-agonist (SABA) reliever therapy to anti-inflammatory reliever (AIR) therapy (ICS-formoterol) in adults and adolescents. While aggregate population-level data indicate increased ICS-formoterol dispensings, patient-level changes in medication use remain unclear. We examined medication use patterns to assess early practice changes across the entire asthma population. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study using the New Zealand national linked health datasets. Patients aged ≥12 with asthma were identified from hospitalisation and/or dispensing data, and categorised by the complete set of inhaler classes dispensed in the three months preceding their final dispensing date within the baseline (July 2018-June 2020) and post-guideline (June 2020-June 2022) periods. Nine mutually exclusive categories were defined without applying any hierarchy between medications: SABA only; ICS, non-formoterol ICS-LABA, and ICS-formoterol, each with and without a concurrently dispensed SABA; other regimens; and no inhaled medication. Age subgroups (12-44 and ≥ 45 years) were examined. Children aged < 12 years throughout follow-up, who were outside the scope of the recommendation, served as a comparison cohort for difference-in-differences estimation. FINDINGS: The cohort included 324,972 patients aged ≥12 years. At baseline, the SABA-only group was the most common (30.5%). Post-guideline, dispensing of the guideline-recommended regimen, ICS-formoterol without SABA, more than doubled from 10.9% to 23.8%, and any ICS-formoterol use rose from 18.9% to 34.5%. The proportion of patients dispensed any SABA fell from 74.1% to 60.8%. Of patients dispensed SABA only pre-guideline, 57.1% were dispensed SABA only again, while 17.6% changed to ICS-formoterol without SABA and 8.1% to ICS-formoterol with SABA. Continuity was high among patients on maintenance therapy (55.9% for ICS, 74.3% for non-formoterol ICS-LABA) and among those already dispensed ICS-formoterol (89.0%). Among post-guideline ICS-formoterol users, 31.1% were also dispensed a SABA, compared with 63.8% of non-formoterol ICS-LABA users and 70.2% of ICS users. Using children aged < 12 years as a comparison cohort, difference-in-differences estimates were +8.4 percentage points for ICS-formoterol without SABA and -8.3 percentage points for total SABA supply, but -0.2 percentage points for SABA monotherapy. INTERPRETATION: The impact of the guideline change was substantial but selective. While the update facilitated transition for patients already receiving maintenance therapy, most patients on SABA-only regimens did not switch to the preferred AIR regimen. Further targeted implementation strategies beyond guideline publication are required to address this gap and ensure evidence-based care is consistently delivered. FUNDING: None.

papers.abstract_en: Activated Cdc42-associated kinase 1 (ACK1; encoded by the TNK2 gene) is an oncogenic protein of the non-receptor tyrosine kinase family and functions downstream of RAS and activated transmembrane receptor tyrosine kinases such as EGFR. Mechanistically, ACK1 inhibition suppresses topoisomerase 2A (Topo IIα; encoded by TOP2A) expression, along with downregulation of the expression of gene sets associated with the regulation of DNA repair and replication, resulting in accumulation of DNA damage and subsequent cellular senescence. Overall, RAS mutation in NSCLC cell lines activates the Cdc42/ACK1 axis, conferring sensitivity to ACK1 inhibition that causes accumulation of DNA damage via inhibition of Topo IIα and DNA repair, G2/M arrest, and eventual cellular senescence in RAS mutant NSCLC cells.

We used pooled ordinary least squares with year fixed effects, Driscoll-Kraay (DK) and small-sample cluster-robust standard errors. RESULTS: In the primary model, listing rates were higher with transplant programme presence (β = +0.86 listings/million/year; 95% DK CI 0.53-1.20), hospital-salaried pulmonologist density (β = +0.066; 95% DK CI 0.02-0.11), and lower socioeconomic deprivation (EDI β = -0.085; 95% DK CI -0.15 to -0.02). Office-based pulmonologist density was associated with listing rates unadjusted but attenuated after adjustment for centre presence, consistent with geographic co-location. With cluster-robust standard errors accounting for correlation within regions, the estimates were unchanged but all confidence intervals included zero. CONCLUSIONS: Inequalities in access to lung transplant listing in France may be in part driven by transplant programme distance, limited hospital-embedded pulmonology, and socioeconomic deprivation. These structural barriers are likely shared by other centralised, single-payer transplant systems. Additional studies using patient-level data to confirm these findings are needed to support interventions targeting these mechanisms.

papers.abstract_en: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) represents the most prevalent form of malignant tumor and constitutes a principal cause of cancer-related mortality globally. Conventional therapeutic approaches predominantly induce apoptosis; however, their efficacy is often compromised by the development of drug resistance. Methuosis, a form of regulated cell death distinct from apoptosis, is characterized by aberrant macropinocytosis and the formation of cytoplasmic vacuoles. Aloperine (ALO), a naturally occurring antitumor alkaloid, has been observed to induce methuosis in cancer cells, although its precise molecular targets and mechanisms remain to be elucidated. This study investigated the anti-NSCLC effects of ALO using cell lines, patient-derived organoids, and mouse xenograft models. Through various assays, it was demonstrated that ALO directly interacts with VPS34 at the I760 residue and promotes TIP60-mediated lactylation of VPS34 at K356 and K781. This interaction inhibits VPS34 kinase activity and reduces intracellular PI(3)P production. The subsequent decrease in PI(3)P levels impedes Armus endosomal recruitment, disrupts Rab7 cycling, leads to the accumulation of macropinosomes, and impairs endolysosomal fusion, ultimately inducing methuosis. ALO exhibits significant antitumor efficacy and acts synergistically with cisplatin to co-activate methuosis and apoptosis, all while avoiding noticeable systemic toxicity. Collectively, ALO targets VPS34 lactylation and disrupts Armus/Rab7 signaling. When used in conjunction with cisplatin, it constitutes a safe and effective therapeutic strategy for NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: KRAS‑mutant non‑small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is heterogeneous, but the subtype‑specific profiles of systemic cytokines and their impact on immunotherapy outcomes remain unclear. METHODS: This retrospective study included 139 patients with KRAS‑mutant NSCLC stratified into G12C (44.6%), G12D (21.6%), and other G12 variants (G12V/A/S/R) (33.8%). Serum levels of seven cytokines (IL‑6, IL‑8, TNF‑α, IL‑10, IL‑17, IL‑1β, IL‑4) were available for 109 patients. Associations with progression‑free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were analyzed using Kaplan‑Meier and Cox regression. RESULTS: Distinct cytokine profiles emerged across subtypes: IL‑10 was elevated in G12C, while IL‑17 was higher in G12D. In the overall ICI‑treated cohort (n = 80), elevated IL‑6, IL‑8, and TNF‑α were associated with worse PFS and OS in univariable analyses. After multivariable adjustment, only IL‑6 remained an independent unfavorable prognostic factor for PFS (adjusted HR = 2.66, p = 0.042). For OS, all three cytokines remained significant after limited adjustment (IL‑6 HR = 2.67, p = 0.050; IL‑8 HR = 5.00, p = 0.049; TNF‑α HR = 2.61, p = 0.037), but findings were exploratory due to not adjusted for multiple testing. In first‑line patients (n = 57), only IL‑6 predicted worse PFS (adjusted HR = 5.34, p = 0.002). Subgroup analysis showed that in G12C (n = 38), IL‑6 and TNF‑α were associated with worse PFS/OS, while in G12D (n = 16), IL‑17 showed a significant association with shorter PFS (log‑rank p = 0.037). No cytokine was prognostic in the G12V/A/S/R subgroup. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that KRAS mutation subtypes may be associated with distinct serum cytokine profiles. IL-6 appeared as a potential subtype-independent negative prognostic factor for PFS, while IL-17 may be relevant in G12D tumors. These observations provide an early rationale for exploring subtype-specific cytokine-targeted strategies, though confirmation in larger prospective cohorts is needed.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) are common toxicities of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but their prognostic implications in older adults remain uncertain. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using SEER-Medicare (2010-2019). We included patients aged ≥66 years with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC who initiated ICI monotherapy or chemoimmunotherapy from 2015-2017. Follow-up began at treatment initiation and continued until death, Medicare disenrollment, or December 31, 2019. The primary exposure was a clinically meaningful irAE, defined as an irAE diagnosis with evidence of systemic immunosuppressant use and/or treatment delay, or discontinuation. In secondary analyses, we categorized patients as having no irAE, an irAE managed without hospitalization, or an irAE requiring hospitalization. The primary outcome was overall survival. We estimated adjusted survival differences and restricted mean survival time using doubly robust causal inference methods. RESULTS: The cohort included 5,304 patients (mean age, 75 years; 52.7% female; 81.9% White). Clinically meaningful irAEs occurred in 1,807 (34.1%) patients, with a median onset of 3.8 months (IQR, 1.1-9.4). Death occurred in 65.1% of patients with irAEs and 78.7% without irAEs, corresponding to an adjusted absolute survival benefit of 6.6% (95% CI, 5.3%-8.0%) and a 6.5-month gain in restricted mean survival time (95% CI, 5.6-7.4). In secondary analyses, irAEs managed without hospitalization showed the greatest benefit (odds ratio [OR], 0.44; 95% CI, 0.35-0.54), whereas irAE hospitalization was associated with attenuated benefit (OR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.89-0.99). CONCLUSIONS: Among older adults with advanced NSCLC receiving ICIs, clinically meaningful irAEs were associated with improved overall survival, particularly when managed without hospitalization. These findings highlight the clinical importance of early recognition of immune-related toxicities; irAE-related hospitalization may identify a higher-risk group warranting closer monitoring and supportive care.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have improved outcomes in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet reliable biomarkers to predict clinical response remain limited. This study aimed to identify and validate a clinically practical biomarker reflecting neoantigen-driven immunogenicity and associated with ICI efficacy in NSCLC. METHODS: We conducted a multi-phase study integrating unbiased discovery, clinical validation, and preliminary mechanistic exploration. Multi-omics profiling of a prospective NSCLC cohort (n = 28) integrated genomics, transcriptomics, and proteomics to identify fibrinogen alpha chain (FGA) as a top candidate. FGA was evaluated by quantitative immunohistochemistry in a training (n = 93) and independent validation (n = 78) cohort of patients with advanced NSCLC treated with ICIs. Multiplex immunofluorescence characterized FGA‑associated immune biology, and in vitro transcriptomic analysis explored transcriptional programs associated with FGA exposure. RESULTS: FGA expression positively correlated with tumor neoantigen expression (r = 0.618, p < 0.001). In the training cohort, high FGA was associated with significantly prolonged progression-free survival (median PFS: 25.8 vs. 5.2 months; adjusted HR = 0.44, p = 0.003) and higher objective response rate (50.0% vs. 30.8%). These findings were confirmed in the independent validation cohort (median PFS: 38.0 vs. 14.4 months; adjusted HR = 0.42, p = 0.017). Exploratory analyses suggested elevated FGA in PD-L1-high tumors and a trend toward prolonged PFS after adjusting for PD-L1 status, though these findings require validation in larger cohorts. Multiplex immunofluorescence revealed significantly higher densities of CD4⁺, CD8⁺, and CD16a⁺ cells in FGA‑high regions (all p < 0.01). Two distinct spatial patterns were identified in both LUSC and LUAD. Pattern I featured direct immune cell infiltration into FGA-enriched regions with closer immune-tumor contact (p < 0.01), whereas Pattern II demonstrated immune concentration within FGA-outlined tumor nests with predominant accumulation on the tumor side. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that FGA exposure was associated with immune activation in both LUSC and LUAD cell lines and additional metabolic reprogramming in LUAD cell lines. CONCLUSIONS: Immunohistochemical assessment of FGA represents a clinically practical biomarker associated with improved outcomes in ICI-treated NSCLC. Preliminary mechanistic exploration suggests that FGA is associated with an immunologically active but histology-dependent tumor microenvironment.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To develop and externally test a multiparametric MRI habitat-based framework integrating intratumoral heterogeneity (ITH), peritumoral heterogeneity (PTH), and clinical characteristics for predicting intracranial progression in patients with EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma and de novo brain metastases receiving first-line third-generation (3rd-gen) EGFR-TKI monotherapy. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study included patients with EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma and de novo brain metastases who received first-line 3rd-gen EGFR-TKI monotherapy. Patients were assigned to an internal training cohort (n = 90) and an external testing cohort (n = 51). The binary prediction outcome was intracranial progression within 20 months after treatment initiation. Pretreatment contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging, T2-weighted imaging, and diffusion-weighted imaging were analyzed. The index brain metastasis and a 6-mm peritumoral region were segmented, followed by voxel-wise habitat clustering. Habitat-specific radiomic features were extracted and selected to construct ITH, PTH, and combined intratumoral-peritumoral habitat (PITH) signatures. Clinical predictors were evaluated using univariable and multivariable logistic regression. Support vector machine models were evaluated using receiver operating characteristic, decision curve, calibration, and Kaplan-Meier analyses. RESULTS: A total of 141 patients were analyzed, including 75 with progressive disease (PD) and 66 without PD (non-PD). Multivariable logistic regression identified EGFR mutation subtype (odds ratio [OR] = 2.390, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.187-4.811, P = 0.015) and the maximum diameter of the index brain metastasis as independent predictors (OR = 2.048, 95% CI: 1.204-3.483, P = 0.008). Models based on imaging heterogeneity features outperformed the clinical model overall. The clinical model achieved an AUC of 0.662, while the ITH, PTH, and PITH models achieved AUCs of 0.715, 0.724, and 0.758, respectively. The combined model showed favorable performance (AUC 0.795, accuracy 76.5%, sensitivity 70.4%, and specificity 83.3%). Patients classified by the combined model as high risk had significantly shorter intracranial progression-free survival (iPFS), than those classified as low risk (log-rank P = 0.019). CONCLUSION: The proposed framework integrating ITH, PTH, and clinical features may provide a noninvasive approach for predicting intracranial progression risk and stratifying prognosis in patients with EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma with newly diagnosed BMs receiving first-line 3rd-gen EGFR-TKI monotherapy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Circulating eosinophils can be measured inexpensively and reproducibly in routine care. Beyond their role in parasite defense and allergy, blood eosinophilia is now a key biomarker in respiratory medicine: prognostic, predictive, and recognized as a "treatable trait." Its role as a marker of susceptibility, however, is not well defined. METHODS: We conducted a monocentric retrospective hospital-based cohort study at Montpellier University Hospital (France), including all adults hospitalized in 2018 with a complete blood count and without prior respiratory disease. Eosinophil counts were stratified as < 150/mm³, 150-299/mm³, and ≥ 300/mm³. The primary outcome was incident respiratory disease, defined by hospitalization with a respiratory diagnosis (ICD-10 J00-J99) or initiation of inhaled therapy (ATC R03). Follow-up extended to December 2024; secondary outcomes included diagnostic subcategories and ICU admission. RESULTS: Among 24,405 patients, 6,173 (25.3%) developed incident respiratory disease. Event rates followed a dose-response pattern across eosinophil strata: 21.7% (< 150/mm³), 26.0% (150-299/mm³), and 32.9% (≥ 300/mm³; p < 0.001 pairwise comparisons across all groups). After multivariable adjustment, eosinophilia remained independently associated with higher risk of developing respiratory disease (HR 1.45, 95% CI 1.35-1.55). Baseline eosinophilia was also associated to increased ICU admissions and greater disease severity during the follow-up. CONCLUSION: Blood eosinophilia was strongly associated with both increased risk of developing incident respiratory disease and in-hospital severity, in a clear dose-response manner. However, most patients with high counts (> 300/mm3) did not develop respiratory events, underscoring the need to integrate blood eosinophil counts with complementary clinical and biological data for risk stratification.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Epidermal growth factor receptor-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs) serve as the standard first-line therapy for advanced EGFR-mutant non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, resistance inevitably restricts their efficacy. Although well-documented acquired resistance mechanisms have been extensively characterized, approximately 30% of patients with EGFR-TKI resistance still present with unknown resistance (UR) mechanisms, and the driving factors behind primary resistance remain inadequately understood. METHODS: In this study, we conducted a large-scale, retrospective cohort study, performing target-capture deep sequencing (>400 genes) on 928 samples from 745 EGFR-TKI-resistant and 183 TKI-naïve EGFR-mutant NSCLC patients. RESULTS: The molecular landscape of EGFR-TKI resistance was systematically characterized. In the resistance cohort, 68.72% (512/745) harbored known resistance (KR) mechanisms, while 31.28% (233/745) were classified as UR. The landscape of KR was significantly influenced by EGFR-TKI generation. First-line third-generation TKI resistance demonstrated fewer EGFR-dependent events compared to first-generation TKIs (p < 0.01) and more RTK and PI3K-AKT-mTOR (PAM) pathway alterations (p < 0.05). In the UR cohort, pathway analysis revealed unique enrichment of atypical pathways, most notably ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling pathways. Differential gene analysis identified significant enrichment of MYC, BRCA1, EPHB, and PTPRD in the UR subgroup. To investigate primary resistance, we found that baseline IKZF1 amplification was significantly enriched in patients with short time-to-treatment-failure (TTF) and correlated with significantly poorer outcomes (HR = 3.02, 95% CI 1.32-6.90; log-rank p = 0.004). CONCLUSIONS: This study provides a comprehensive real-world landscape of EGFR-TKI resistance, demonstrating distinct mechanisms influenced by TKI generation. ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling was identified as a distinctive pathway feature of unknown resistance, and baseline IKZF1 amplification emerged as a candidate biomarker of EGFR-TKI primary resistance. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Platinum-etoposide plus a programmed death-ligand 1 inhibitor is standard first-line therapy for extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC). Febrile neutropenia (FN) is a frequent adverse event. Primary granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) prophylaxis may reduce FN but also modulate antitumor immunity. We examined whether primary G-CSF prophylaxis reduced FN without compromising chemoimmunotherapy efficacy. METHODS: This Japanese multicenter, retrospective observational study enrolled patients with ES-SCLC or relapsed limited-stage SCLC treated with platinum-etoposide plus atezolizumab or durvalumab. The primary endpoint was FN incidence during first-line therapy. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and propensity score matching (PSM) were used for primary and sensitivity analyses, respectively. RESULTS: Among 285 patients, 64 received primary G-CSF prophylaxis (pegylated G-CSF administration in cycle 1). In IPTW analyses comparing the primary and non-primary G-CSF prophylaxis groups, the former was associated with lower FN incidence (2.6% vs. 28.6%; odds ratio [OR], 0.07; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.02-0.30), fewer FN-related emergency visits (1.6% vs. 16.1%) and admissions (1.6% vs. 15.3%), and higher average relative dose intensity (0.76 vs. 0.71). Objective response rate was 65.7% vs. 73.1% (OR, 0.71; 95% CI: 0.36-1.42), median progression-free survival was 4.8 vs. 5.1 months (hazard ratio [HR], 0.88; 95% CI: 0.63-1.22), and median overall survival was 14.2 vs. 13.2 months (HR, 0.79; 95% CI: 0.55-1.13), without any differences between the groups. PSM findings were comparable. CONCLUSIONS: Primary G-CSF prophylaxis during first-line SCLC chemoimmunotherapy was associated with lower FN incidence and FN-related acute-care use, without evidence of compromised antitumor efficacy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Tezepelumab is a monoclonal antibody approved in the United States for severe asthma. Real-world evidence of effectiveness remains limited. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effectiveness of tezepelumab in reducing annualized asthma exacerbation rates (AAERs) and healthcare resource utilization (HRU) in the United States. METHODS: This retrospective, self-controlled, pre-post cohort study used data from Symphony Health, an ICON plc Company, PatientSource®, December 1, 2020, to June 30, 2024. Eligible patients were ≥12 years, had ≥2 records of tezepelumab, and experienced ≥2 asthma exacerbations in the 12 months before tezepelumab initiation, with index date being the day after initiation. AAERs and asthma exacerbation-related HRU were compared between the 12 months pre- and post-index. AAERs were also evaluated across patient subgroups. RESULTS: A total of 527 patients were included. AAERs decreased significantly from 2.81 to 1.26 per person-year (55% decrease; 95% confidence interval [CI] [51%, 59%]; p<0.001). The greatest benefit was observed among patients starting treatment February 2023 and later (61% decrease; [53%-67%]; p<0.001). Consistent reductions were seen across subgroups: patients with pre-index blood eosinophil count <300 cells/μL and ≥300 cells/μL, pre-index total serum immunoglobulin E levels <100 IU/mL and ≥100 IU/mL, biologic-naïve and biologic-experienced, persistent tezepelumab users, and those with comorbid chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyposis. Asthma exacerbation-related HRU declined significantly (p<0.001) with 50-54% reductions across healthcare settings. CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world study, patients with severe asthma treated with tezepelumab had substantial reductions in asthma exacerbations and HRU, with the greatest benefits among more recent initiators.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is a chronic, life-limiting genetic disease. Treatment with CFTR modulators (CFTRm), such as the triple combination therapies elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (ELX/TEZ/IVA) and vanzacaftor/tezacaftor/deutivacaftor (VNZ/TEZ/D-IVA), have significantly improved clinical outcomes and quality of life for many people with CF. While most individuals treated with CFTRm report no change or improvement in neuropsychiatric symptoms, a minority have reported new or worsening symptoms. This has led to hypotheses that CFTRm or CFTR function could have relationships to neuropsychiatric symptoms. METHODS: To evaluate potential off-target or on-target effects of CFTRm and/or CFTR function on neuropsychiatric symptoms, we conducted four independent analyses: (a) in vitro off-target screening at clinically-relevant free concentrations; (b) nonclinical, in vivo behavioral pharmacology studies; (c) analysis of clinical trial and real-world evidence of CFTRm neuropsychiatric adverse events; and (d) human genetic analysis of CFTR functional variants in ∼1 million individuals diagnosed with neuropsychiatric disorders. RESULTS: No off-target effects of ELX, VNZ, TEZ, or IVA were observed in vitro at clinically-relevant free concentrations, nor were any behavioral findings observed in vivo animal studies. Up to date analysis of clinical trial and real-world data covering >250,000 patient-years of experience with CFTRm did not show any increase in risk of neuropsychiatric adverse events. Human genetic analyses of functional CFTR variants did not identify association with any of 23 neuropsychiatric conditions. CONCLUSIONS: Multiple independent lines of investigation failed to show any evidence for off-target or on-target effects of CFTRm and/or CFTR function on neuropsychiatric symptoms.

papers.abstract_en: UNLABELLED: Influenza virus replication relies on coordinated assembly of ribonucleoprotein (RNP) complexes in the nucleus, yet how host long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) regulate this process remains poorly defined. Here, we identify the lncRNA AL645608.7 as a potent antiviral factor and show that its two splice variants restrict influenza replication. Mechanistically, AL645608.7 contains eight tandem 66-nt repeats that recruit the RNA-binding protein PTBP1, primarily through PTBP1's RRM3 domain. The AL645608.7-PTBP1 assembly then engages key viral RNP components-PB2 and NP-and functionally disrupts the PB2-NP interface, thereby suppressing viral RNA synthesis. Domain-mapping analyses further distinguish the regions responsible for PTBP1 recruitment from those involved in PB2 and NP engagement, demonstrating that distinct structural elements of AL645608.7 coordinate host-protein recruitment and viral RNP interference. Importantly, lipid nanoparticle delivery of AL645608.7 markedly reduces viral burden and improves disease outcomes in mice, providing a proof-of-concept nucleic-acid therapeutic strategy. Together, our findings reveal a repeat-programmed lncRNA mechanism that rewires a host RNA-binding protein to dismantle influenza RNP organization and support the therapeutic potential of lncRNA-based intervention against influenza virus infection. IMPORTANCE: This study identified that influenza virus infection significantly upregulated the long noncoding RNA (lncRNA) AL645608.7. Both of its transcripts, AL645608.7-v1 and AL645608.7-v2, exhibited antiviral activity against influenza virus. Mechanistically, AL645608.7 was shown to directly bind to the host protein PTBP1. Furthermore, the nuclear-localized AL645608.7 recruits PTBP1 via a 66-base repeat motif. Importantly, PTBP1 interacts with both the N- and C-terminal regions of the influenza virus polymerase subunit PB2 as well as the NP, thereby disrupting the NP-PB2 interaction. The AL645608.7-PTBP1 complex amplifies this inhibitory effect, ultimately impairing vRNA synthesis and blocking efficient viral replication. These findings offer novel insights into the functional role of noncoding RNAs in host-influenza virus interactions.

papers.abstract_en: Aspergillus fumigatus is a major opportunistic fungal pathogen and an important cause of invasive aspergillosis in immunocompromised patients. Azole antifungals remain central to treatment, but azole resistance is increasingly reported. Azole resistance in A. fumigatus is often linked to canonical cyp51A mechanisms, but many resistant isolates lack these mutations, suggesting additional contributions. This study analysed 12 newly sequenced azole-susceptible clinical isolates from KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, together with publicly available clinical and environmental A. fumigatus genomes using a uniform AF293 reference-based workflow for variant calling, population structure correction and genome wide association studies (GWAS). A filtered SNP-alignment matrix was used to infer population structure and perform structure-aware genome-wide association testing with azole susceptibility status as a binary phenotype. Overall, 194 of 227 genomes met predefined quality thresholds, and 31 949 biallelic SNPs were tested using ten PCoA axes as covariates. After adjustment using SNP-derived PCoA covariates, 16 SNPs exceeded the Bonferroni threshold and 206 SNPs passed BH-FDR correction. The strongest association signals were distributed across multiple genomic regions rather than being restricted to a single canonical resistance locus, with candidate annotations linked to sterol and lipid metabolism, membrane transport, transcriptional regulation, cell-wall remodelling and stress response. Transporter-focused analysis showed that all 12 South African isolates had negative CDR1 and MFS transporter-balance scores, placing them among the most transporter-depleted susceptible backgrounds in the dataset. Phylogenetic reconstruction showed interspersed resistant and susceptible isolates, supporting repeated emergence or local amplification rather than expansion of a single resistant clone. Overall, these findings support a cautious model in which azole resistance-associated variation in A. fumigatus is distributed across multiple functional pathways within a structured population background. The South African isolates provide a local susceptible clinical baseline for future expanded surveillance.Keywords: Aspergillus fumigatus, Azole resistance, Genome Wide Association, SNPs.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Bacteriophage carry-over, the continued lytic activity of residual phages after experimental sampling, poses a significant challenge in bacteriophage research, potentially skewing experimental results, particularly in the context of preclinical studies where perceived laboratory success may not translate clinically. These inaccuracies, relevant across various bacterial species, underscore the necessity for robust mitigation strategies. This study provides an overview of strategies to mitigate phage carry-over, evaluating their performance on a combination of three mycobacteriophages with lytic activity against M. tuberculosis. RESULTS: We investigated three inactivation methods, including ferrous ammonium sulfate (FAS) and citrate for in vitro applications and N-acetyl-L-cysteine-sodium hydroxide (NALC-NaOH) for sputum decontamination. The citrate buffer offered limited and specific phage inactivation, but FAS was effective in inactivating all three mycobacteriophages (FionnbharthΔ45Δ47, Muddy HRMN0157-2, and Fred313cpm-1Δ33). With pH adapted to 5.0, FAS did not significantly reduce M. tuberculosis H37Rv viability after five minutes exposure. Phage carry-over was determined to be phage-dependent; FionnbharthΔ45Δ47 exhibited the most significant reduction in M. smegmatis colony forming units without phage inactivation measures. Furthermore, we showed that NALC-NaOH methods, commonly used for sputum decontamination, are highly effective in reducing phage titers in aqueous solutions and human sputum samples. CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates the heterogenous and phage-dependent efficacy of available inactivation buffers, underscoring the critical necessity for researchers to empirically screen their specific phage isolates against chosen inactivation methods. This is crucial to ensure that observed antibacterial effects are correctly attributed to phage activity during the experimental period, rather than to uncontrolled phage carry-over, thereby enhancing the reliability and interpretability of results.

papers.abstract_en: AIMS: Pulmonary sclerosing pneumocytoma (PSP) combined with carcinoid is rare, and the potential pathogenetic relationship between the two tumor components is unclear. METHODS AND RESULTS: We collected six cases from three institutions in China (2020-2023), evaluated histopathological and immunophenotypic features, and performed a review of the literature. In contrast, of the three patients with spatially separated biphasic lesions, only Case 1 bore the variant exclusively in its PSP compartment, corresponding to the seventh positive compartment (1/12), whereas the matched carcinoid component lacked this variant entirely. After RNA extraction and library quality control, four PSP samples (Cases 1, 2, 4, 5) and three carcinoid samples (Cases 1, 2, 4) were retained; transcriptomic profiling further revealed that, in these eligible cases, the expression patterns of key marker genes (i.e., SYP, NCAM1, and NKX2-1) were highly consistent with the immunohistochemical findings, and that both components shared activation of major oncogenic signaling pathways, including the PI3K/Akt pathway. papers.abstract_en: Lung transplantation (LTx) remains the only definitive therapy for selected patients with end-stage lung disease, yet outcomes are limited by early ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) and primary graft dysfunction (PGD), and by chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD) as the leading cause of late graft failure. These entities share overlapping injury and repair pathways, including alveolocapillary barrier disruption, microvascular dysfunction, innate immune activation, and maladaptive remodeling, which remain incompletely controlled by current perioperative management and systemic immunosuppression. This review summarizes cell and gene therapy approaches in LTx and frames these strategies around the IRI/PGD-to-CLAD continuum. Stromal cell therapies, regulatory immune cell approaches, and cell-free or cell-derived products such as extracellular vesicles and mitochondrial transfer are discussed, with emphasis on route, dose, persistence, and the graft microenvironment as determinants of biological activity. Gene modulation strategies and delivery platforms relevant to the lung, including viral vectors, lipid nanoparticles, and virus-like particles, are outlined, together with preclinical gene therapy strategies targeting IRI and allograft rejection. Ex vivo lung perfusion (EVLP) is highlighted as a practical window for organ-confined delivery and early mechanistic assessment prior to implantation. Key translational considerations are outlined, including product characterization and potency, clinically interpretable dosing, and the need for harmonized endpoints and pharmacodynamic readouts to improve comparability across studies.

papers.abstract_en: Management of drug-resistant bacterial pneumonia has become increasingly precise, but early precision does not remove the need to reinterpret the patient's course during illness. Active and appropriate empirical therapy, informed by local epidemiology, remains essential, yet treatment often begins before the definitive microbiological profile is available or adequate drug exposure can be confirmed. While rapid diagnostics and pharmacological optimisation can narrow this initial uncertainty, the harder problem arises when antimicrobial treatment appears plausible but the patient shows delayed improvement, clinical deterioration, or incomplete recovery. These trajectories should not be treated as a single form of antibiotic failure. Instead, they require reassessment of whether the dominant limitation is persistent infection, inadequate drug exposure, dysregulated host response, a non-infectious mimic, or repair-limited recovery. In this Review, we propose a trajectory-guided conceptual framework that links management to the process most likely to limit recovery and distinguishes clinically implementable interventions from emerging translational concepts.

papers.abstract_en: High-Flow Nasal Cannula (HFNC) is a critical tool for respiratory support in acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and for subjects with general hypoxemia; however, pharmaceutical aerosol delivery simultaneous with HFNC support is known to be highly inefficient. The aim of this study was to develop and validate a high-fidelity, complete-airway computational fluid dynamics (CA-CFD) model of regional aerosol deposition that occurs when a pharmaceutical aerosol product is administered through a nasal interface simultaneously with HFNC therapy. The CFD model included the aerosol delivery tubing and interface connected to a complete-airway (CA) model extending from the extrathoracic nose-throat (NT) region through the conducting airways and alveoli. CFD-predicted regional aerosol deposition was compared with previously published in vivo experimental data. Predictions of the CA-CFD model agreed closely with the available cohort-level human-subject in vivo data including a predicted aerosol deposition fraction in the lungs of 2.9% (based on nebulized dose) compared with in vivo medians of 2.1% (gamma scintigraphy; range: 1.5-2.9%) and 3.7% (SPECT-CT; range: 2.2-4.7%). In addition to low lung delivery efficiency, the regional drug delivery showed high heterogeneity. Considering a map of regional airway deposition, utilizing a realistic polydisperse droplet size distribution in the stochastic individual path (SIP) models, deposition fractions in the NT, upper tracheobronchial (TB), middle TB, lower TB and alveolar regions were 16%, 0.5%, 0.1%, 0.1%, and 2.4% of the nebulized dose, with ∼ 22% of the nebulized dose exhaled/escaped/dripped, while ∼ 58% was lost in the HFNC circuit. Through methodical development, a CA-CFD model of aerosol delivery during HFNC therapy was established that closely agrees with the in vivo cohort-level data and can now serve as a "representative population-level digital twin" to optimize aerosol delivery during this highly challenging but clinically popular mode of ventilation support.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Acute lung injury (ALI) is a life-threatening inflammatory pulmonary disorder characterized by excessive inflammation, oxidative stress, and disruption of lung tissue integrity. Macrophage dysregulation plays a critical role in the progression of ALI, making macrophage modulation a potential therapeutic strategy. Tectorigenin (Tec), a natural isoflavonoid with anti-inflammatory activity, has shown protective effects in inflammatory disorders, but its underlying mechanism and macrophage-targeted delivery in ALI remain unclear. Here, we developed a macrophage membrane-camouflaged MOF818 nanozyme for macrophage-targeted delivery of Tec, termed T-M@MM, to enhance its therapeutic efficacy against ALI. METHODS: The effects of Tec and T-M@MM were evaluated in LPS-induced ALI mice and LPS- or TBHP-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages. Macrophage depletion, network pharmacology, molecular docking, and cellular thermal shift assay were used to investigate the underlying mechanisms. Macrophage polarization, glycolysis, oxidative stress, mitochondrial function, and apoptosis were assessed using molecular and cellular assays. The physicochemical properties, Tec loading and release profiles, macrophage uptake, pulmonary biodistribution, biosafety, and therapeutic efficacy of T-M@MM were further evaluated. RESULTS: Tec alleviated pulmonary inflammation and oxidative stress and promoted an anti-inflammatory macrophage phenotype, whereas macrophage depletion attenuated these effects. PFKFB3 was identified as a potential molecular target associated with the effects of Tec, and Tec suppressed PFKFB3-associated glycolysis and promoted anti-inflammatory macrophage polarization, which was attenuated by PFKFB3 overexpression. T-M@MM enabled Tec loading and exhibited pH/ROS-responsive release, enhanced macrophage uptake and pulmonary retention (>48 h), and potent ROS-scavenging activity. In LPS-induced ALI mice, T-M@MM alleviated pulmonary inflammation, oxidative stress, edema, and pathological injury without obvious abnormalities in major-organ histology, liver or kidney function, or body weight. CONCLUSION: T-M@MM integrates macrophage targeting, ROS scavenging, and Tec-mediated modulation of PFKFB3-associated glycolysis to regulate macrophage responses and ameliorate LPS-induced ALI, with preliminary evidence of favorable biocompatibility, providing a potential macrophage-targeted nanotherapeutic strategy.

papers.abstract_en: Distal lung delivery remains a key bottleneck for inhaled therapy in severe pulmonary disease. We developed a hydrogen-oxygen mixture (H2/O2 mixture, 2:1 v/v) gas-assisted nebulization platform to deliver ROS-responsive, self-assembled methylprednisolone dimer nanoparticles (MP2-TK NPs). MP2-TK NPs were stable during nebulization and selectively released drug under ROS-rich conditions. Compared with air, H2/O2 mixture improved NGI-assessed aerosol deposition and artificial mucus penetration. CFD simulations further supported enhanced distal deposition, particularly for clinically respirable droplets (1-5 μm). In an LPS-induced acute lung injury mouse model, H2/O2-assisted nebulization increased pulmonary distribution and small-airway localization of MP2-TK NPs, leading to reduced bronchoalveolar lavage cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β), total cell counts, and protein levels. H2/O2 mixture inhalation alone also showed anti-inflammatory activity, consistent with hydrogen's antioxidant effects. This strategy couples carrier-gas engineering with ROS-responsive nanomedicine to enhance deep-lung delivery and therapeutic efficacy in acute lung injury.

papers.abstract_en: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) is a chronic and progressive interstitial lung disease with a poor prognosis and limited therapeutic options. Current antifibrotic therapies only slow disease progression, underscoring an urgent need for novel therapeutic strategies. In recent years, metabolic reprogramming, notably the shift towards aerobic glycolysis (the Warburg effect), has emerged as a key driver of PF pathogenesis. This review comprehensively examines the central role of glycolysis in fueling the fibrotic cascade. It summarizes the major risk factors and fundamental pathogenic mechanisms of PF. The review then delves into the molecular mechanisms by which profibrotic signals, such as TGF‑β1, remodel cellular metabolism. The upregulation and pathogenic roles of critical glycolytic nodes are detailed‑including glucose transporters, hexokinase 2, phosphofructokinase‑2/fructose‑2,6‑bisphosphatase 3, pyruvate kinase M2 and lactate dehydrogenase A‑in activated fibroblasts, injured epithelial cells and pro‑fibrotic immune cells. Furthermore, the interplay between glycolysis and key signaling pathways (TGF‑β1, hypoxia‑inducible factor‑1α, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, Hippo, AMP‑activated protein kinase and sirtuins) that form feed‑forward loops to sustain the fibrotic process is discussed. Furthermore, therapeutic strategies targeting glycolytic enzymes and upstream metabolic checkpoints are highlighted, summarizing preclinical evidence for small‑molecule inhibitors and non‑coding RNAs as emerging regulators of glycolytic reprogramming. By consolidating current knowledge on glycolysis‑centric metabolic underpinnings of PF, this review underscores the promise of metabolism‑based interventions and discusses challenges for translating these findings into effective therapies.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Epidemiological studies have shown that fine particulate matter (PM) is closely associated with increased morbidity and mortality from lung diseases. However, the mechanisms by which PM affects alveolar epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), such as mitochondrial dysfunction, remain unclear, and therapy options require further investigation. METHODS: Human type II alveolar epithelial cells (A549 cells) were exposed to 100 µg/mL PM to investigate EMT induction. In an animal model, mice were exposed to PM via intratracheal injection to simulate air pollution exposure. RESULTS: PM exposure reduced the expression of the epithelial marker E-cadherin while increasing the expression of mesenchymal markers vimentin, α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA), and transforming growth factor β1 (TGF-β1). Furthermore, the expression of EMT-related transcription factors Snail and Slug was upregulated, accompanied by a morphological shift in A549 cells from cubic to spindle shapes and enhanced cell migration. PM also promoted mitochondrial fission and induced the accumulation of LC3B and p62 proteins. Treatment with the antifibrotic drug pirfenidone (PFD) effectively reduced PM-induced EMT-related protein expression and cell migration. These effects are achieved by reducing mitochondrial fission, increasing autophagosome accumulation, and related autophagic degradation. The lungs of PM-treated mice showed increased expression of EMT-related proteins, significant blood cell infiltration, and alveolar wall thickening. PFD treatment significantly improved these conditions and reduced collagen deposition. CONCLUSION: PM induces increased mitochondrial fission and incomplete autophagy (characterized by autophagosome accumulation and impaired flux), leading to EMT. PFD treatment can also effectively reduce PM-induced EMT formation by modulating these pathways.

papers.abstract_en: Despite significant advances in ex vivo machine perfusion and innovation in graft modulation, successful translation of preclinical research into clinical practice is limited by the lack of multi-disciplinary exchange early in the research pipeline. LifeLUNG is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network funded by the European Union that aims to improve long-term outcomes in lung transplantation by leveraging ex vivo lung perfusion platforms to genetically modify donor lungs to modulate immune responses, reduce injury, and prevent graft rejection. LifeLUNG introduces an ELSA-IE approach, integrating Ethical, Legal, and Social Aspects research, Implementation science, and health Economics with preclinical research to navigate translational uncertainties and reduce the risk of late-stage innovation failure. By fostering the continuous exchange of insights and challenges among researchers, patients, and health systems, LifeLUNG aims to accelerate the responsible and clinically viable translation of lung transplantation innovations.

papers.abstract_en: As one of the first oral antivirals authorized for outpatient treatment of COVID-19, molnupiravir (Lagevrio) illustrates the complex interplay among emergency regulatory frameworks, clinical trial evidence, and real-world outcomes. This narrative review synthesizes evidence from pivotal trials (MOVe-OUT, PANORAMIC), global genomic surveillance datasets, regulatory filings, and pharmacokinetic barrier studies to examine how eight interlocking U.S. statutory and administrative instruments compressed development timelines while sustaining product availability. Molnupiravir induces lethal mutagenesis in SARS-CoV-2; the FDA granted Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) in December 2021 based on interim data showing approximately a 50% reduction in hospitalization or death. Final trial analyses lowered this estimate to roughly 30%, and the large-scale PANORAMIC trial found no reduction in hospitalization or mortality among highly vaccinated populations. Emerging safety concerns-including teratogenicity, juvenile skeletal toxicity, and a molnupiravir-associated mutational signature detected across global viral genomic databases-further eroded its benefit-risk profile, contributing to the European Medicines Agency's 2023 refusal of marketing authorization and to the drug's lack of full FDA approval. Existing statutory frameworks nonetheless preserve molnupiravir's EUA status as a second-line option for high-risk patients. Its trajectory highlights the tension between emergency speed and long-term pharmacovigilance and offers actionable, One Health-informed lessons for pandemic-preparedness legislation.

papers.abstract_en: Innate immune activation is critical for mounting protective host immune responses against viral infections. Viruses have evolved mechanisms to counteract host innate immune responses and restrict host defence. Intriguingly, growing evidence suggests that RNA viruses of zoonotic origin, particularly influenza viruses, trigger dysregulated innate immune activation leading to excessive inflammation and cellular damage. However, the host and viral mechanisms underlying the dysregulated innate immune responses that cause severe immunopathology remain to be fully unravelled. In this review, we discuss how aberrant RNA sensing contributes to innate immune responses during highly pathogenic influenza infections. We also discuss perspectives on influenza viral polymerase compatibility with host factors and species-specific RNA-sensing mechanisms as critical determinants of the pathological outcome during highly pathogenic influenza infections.

papers.abstract_en: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is one of the leading causes of death globally. It is characterized by irreversible airway obstruction and alveolar abnormalities. The pathogenesis of COPD is complex, involving multiple cell types in lung tissue and multifactorial processes, including cellular inflammatory responses. In recent years, pyroptosis-a novel form of cell death-has been closely linked to the development of COPD. Pyroptosis is defined by cell membrane rupture and the release of pro-inflammatory cellular contents. Importantly, the mechanisms of pyroptosis vary among different cell types in COPD. Non-coding RNAs, including microRNAs (miRNAs), circular RNAs (circRNAs), and long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), play a crucial role in modulating pyroptosis in COPD. These molecules can directly modulate pyroptosis or indirectly influence it through the competitive endogenous RNA (ceRNA) network. This article reviews the current research progress on the expression patterns and pathological roles of miRNAs, circRNAs, lncRNAs, and ceRNAs in different cell types of COPD. These studies provide a new perspective for understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying COPD and offer a scientific basis for developing novel prevention, diagnostic, and therapeutic strategies. Looking ahead, future research will focus on leveraging individual differences in non-coding RNAs to develop personalized COPD treatment strategies. This approach has the potential to enhance therapeutic efficacy and reduce adverse reactions, ultimately improving patient outcomes.
